data.taskBrief:
TASK BRIEF: Send a transactional email to a customer using the Sendinblue API

FIT
  Fully. The supplied request sends a transactional email, which covers the stated email capability. The broader support goal also mentions resolving order, refund, and status questions, but no supplied request serves those separate capabilities; this email request is the only relevant request, and the saved bad-request example is not an additional request.

AUTH
  API key authentication. Send the credential in the `api-key` header as the value of `{{send_in_blue_api_key}}` (or your actual Sendinblue API key).

BASE URL
  https://api.sendinblue.com/v3

STEPS
  1. POST /smtp/email
     Params (JSON body):
       sender: object — `{ "name": "Mary from MyShop", "email": "no-reply@myshop.com" }`; include the sender object in the body.
       sender.name: string — `'Mary from MyShop'`; body field within `sender`.
       sender.email: string — `'no-reply@myshop.com'`; body field within `sender`.
       to: array of objects — `[{ "email": "customer@example.com", "name": "Customer" }]`; body field containing the customer recipient.
       to[].email: string — `'customer@example.com'`; body field within each recipient object.
       to[].name: string — `'Customer'`; body field within each recipient object.
       templateId: integer — `69`; body field selecting the transactional template.
       Also accepts: bcc, cc, htmlContent, textContent, subject, replyTo, attachment, headers, params, messageVersions, tags, scheduledAt, batchId — see the request schema for details.
       Headers: `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: application/json`.
     Returns:
       201 Created with a JSON `messageId` string for a sent email; the examples also show 202 Accepted with a JSON `messageId` for a scheduled email, 200 OK with an empty body for a batch example, and 400 Bad Request with `code` and `message` fields for an invalid request.
     Threading:
       None

GOTCHAS
  - Resolve `{{baseUrl}}` to `https://api.sendinblue.com/v3` and replace `{{send_in_blue_api_key}}` with the actual API key.
  - Send the body as JSON and preserve the nested `sender` and `to` structures.
  - Use a customer’s actual email and optional name in `to`; the saved recipient is only an example.
  - `templateId` is shown as an integer; use the intended transactional template ID.
  - A successful send returns `messageId`; a scheduled-send response may be `202 Accepted` rather than `201 Created`.
